run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:50:02Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for service frontend-proxy (namespace otel-demo) corresponds to an observed burst of frontend-proxy ingress spans with error=true / http.status_code 504 / otel.status_code ERROR, each lasting about 15.0 s, and to frontend-proxy log lines of the form '"GET /api/recommendations?productIds=... HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 14999/15000/15001'. The sampled error traces show the 504 is generated at the proxy while the frontend handler for /api/recommendations is still running: in trace 1b22375ef202bc584afc76532e269fd9 the load-generator GET and the frontend-proxy ingress both ended at 15.0 s with 504, while the frontend '/api/recommendations' span took 22.08 s and returned 200 and its grpc client span to oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations took 22.079 s. Recommendation's own server-side p95 for /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations rose from ~72-75 ms (08:45-08:48) to 194 ms (08:49), 460 ms (08:50), 710 ms (08:51) and 917 ms (08:52). In the same period, Chaos Mesh events show a Schedule named otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress in namespace chaos-mesh spawning a new StressChaos object every minute from 08:46:58 to 08:54:58, and each sparse object's events record 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation' followed by TimeUp/Recovered about 55 s later. The recommendation pod and the frontend-proxy pod were both Running and ready with 0 restarts. The evidence therefore points to CPU stress injected into the single recommendation pod as the origin of the latency, with the frontend-proxy 504s being the downstream symptom of its 15 s upstream response timeout, but the StressChaos/Schedule specs themselves could not be read, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans in the incident window are ingress spans with status_tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR", duration_us about 15,000,000 (15 s); the paired 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true" and http.status_code="0", and their visible parent is a load-generator GET span.

frontend-proxy container logs (pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p8qtl) contain 504 responses with flag 'UT response_timeout' only on GET /api/recommendations, with upstream response times of 14999-15001 ms, observed at 08:49:37, 08:49:38, 08:49:38, 08:50:26, 08:50:27 and 08:50:28 and again at 08:51:36 through 08:55:26 (newest 20 of 50 matching lines in 08:45-08:57).

frontend-proxy error-span counts (increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} over 300 s, not a per-second rate and not a request count) rose from 0 at 08:50 and 1.11 at 08:51 to 7.78 (08:52), 12.2 (08:53), 28.9 (08:54), 43.3 (08:55), peak 44.4 (08:56), then fell to 31.1 (08:57), 20 (08:58), 18.9 (08:59), 7.58 (09:00), 4.46 (09:01) and 0 (09:02). ad, cart, frontend, payment and recommendation stayed at 0-1.11 in the same series.

The all-span error ratio for service frontend-proxy (rate of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans / rate of all spans, 5 m window) was at or below 0.00019 through 08:50 and then rose to 0.00135 (08:51), 0.00220 (08:52), 0.00542 (08:53), 0.00832 (08:54), 0.00866 (08:56) and back to 0 at 09:02.

histogram_quantile(0.95) of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket for service_name="recommendation", span_name="/oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER" was 72.8-74.6 ms at 08:45-08:48, then 194 ms (08:49), 460 ms (08:50), 710 ms (08:51) and 917 ms (08:52); from 08:53 onward the expression returned NaN (undefined), which leaves later tail latency unknown rather than proven higher.

In trace 1b22375ef202bc584afc76532e269fd9 the load-generator GET span (15.002 s, http.status_code 504) parents the frontend-proxy ingress span (15.0006 s, 504, otel.status_code ERROR); the frontend span 'GET /api/recommendations' ran 22.082 s and returned http.status_code 200, and the frontend client span grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations ran 22.079 s with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, while product-catalog spans in the same trace took 65-191 microseconds.

Since 08:46:58 a Schedule named otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress in namespace chaos-mesh emitted Spawned events each minute (creating otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-jn58v, -gwd9j, -tq59h, -lwlmp, -h7zr7, -6p484, -vmtj8, -flf8h, -q55wg) through 08:54:58.

Each spawned StressChaos object (e.g. otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress-jn58v at 08:46:58, -h7zr7 at 08:50:58, -q55wg at 08:54:58) emitted Started/Applied events with message 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation', then TimeUp ('Time up according to the duration') about 55 s later and Recovered ('Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv/recommendation').

At query time the pods frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p8qtl and recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv (the StressChaos target) were both Running, ready=true with 0 restarts; the frontend-proxy container has no previous (crashed) instance.

Some error spans exist in other services but at much lower volume: ad held about 1.11 error spans per 5 m at 08:37-08:40 (before the incident) and again at 08:52-08:55, fraud-detection held 1.11 at 08:55-08:58, and recommendation 1.11 at 08:45 and 08:48-08:51; these are not on the /api/recommendations 504 path described above.

The pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-dz8j9 recorded 3 BackOff events between 08:25:26 and 08:29:50 and its container was restarted (last Started 08:30:05); its restartCount is 3. This happened before the frontend-proxy error signal began deviating at about 08:49-08:51.

The CPU stress that the Chaos Mesh Schedule otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress applied repeatedly to pod otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv (container recommendation) slowed oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations; the frontend handler for /api/recommendations consequently exceeded the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream response timeout, producing the 504 UT response_timeout errors counted by the alert. The mechanism matches the observed settings (chaos applied from 08:46:58, recommendation p95 rising from 08:49, 504s from ~08:49, chaos TimeUp at ~08:54-08:55 and error counts decaying to 0 by 09:02), but causality is inferred from timing and path correlation, not from a read StressChaos spec.

Rejected: frontend-proxy failing on its own (crash, restart or misconfiguration). Its pod was Running/ready with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, and its 504 lines are the programmed upstream response timeout ('UT response_timeout', 14999-15001 ms) on one route while other routes (/api/cart, /api/products, /api/data, /api/checkout) continued to return 200/308 in the same log sample.

Rejected: the recommendation latency came from product-catalog as the slow dependency. In the affected trace the product-catalog spans (oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and ListProducts) took 65-191 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, while the frontend's client call to RecommendationService/ListRecommendations took 22.079 s.

The frontend service itself recorded 0 status_code ERROR spans in every 5 m bucket from 08:35 to 09:02 (increase over 300 s = 0), and the affected frontend '/api/recommendations' span returned http.status_code 200; the errors counted by the alert are on the frontend-proxy side, not produced by frontend error responses.

gaps: The alerting rule definition for RequestErrorRate was not retrievable (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data), so the expression producing the reported 'current: 0.06666666666666667' could not be reproduced; the highest 5 m all-span error ratio I computed for frontend-proxy was 0.00866 at 08:56, which indicates a different denominator/aggregation is used by the rule.

The Chaos Mesh Schedule and StressChaos specs (stressor type/cpu load, workers, duration, selector mode) could not be read because chaos-mesh custom resources are not in the permitted Kubernetes resource list; the CPU-stress nature, target pod otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv and container recommendation are known only from object names and Normal event messages.
recommendation's server-side p95 became undefined (NaN) from 08:53 onward, so the full latency tail during the peak of the incident is unknown, not measured.
The earliest 504 line is unknown: in window 08:44:00-08:50:30 the newest 6 of 10 matching 504 lines were shown starting 08:49:37, and 4 earlier lines were not read.

Error-tag trace searches for ad and fraud-detection in 08:50-09:02 returned no matching traces (no_data), so the nature of their sporadic error spans (about 1 per 5 min) is unknown; Jaeger holds only a sampled, recent set of traces.
In trace 1b22375ef202bc584afc76532e269fd9 no recommendation server span is visible (only the frontend client span of 22.079 s), so that individual request's server-side duration is unknown.
Kubernetes objects and events are snapshots at query time and events expire; the chaos-mesh event list ends at 08:54:58, so scheduling behaviour after that moment is unknown.
next_steps: Read the Schedule/Schedule spec of chaos-mesh/otel-demo-recommendation-cpu-stress and the spawned StressChaos objects (stressors.cpu, duration, target selector) with elevated read permission to confirm the injected CPU load and target.
Check container CPU throttling/usage for pod otel-demo/recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv during 08:46-08:56 and confirm the recommendation latency recovers after the chaos experiments stop.
Review whether the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream response timeout is intentionally configured for the /api/recommendations route and align the frontend/recommendation timeouts.
Inspect the fraud-detection pod's earlier restart/BackOff (08:25-08:29) and its 08:55-08:58 error spans separately; they are not explained by this investigation.
